title: Reuniting Once Again
text: While I waited like that… a carriage driven by a familiar-looking demi-human came clip-clopping toward the fort. Squinting, I could see that Father appeared to be aboard. It didn’t seem like anything in particular had gone wrong, I say.
“Wait just a moment, if you would!”
I swiftly canceled my concealment and stepped out in front of the carriage, raising a hand.
“Oh…? You’re the Spear Hero.”
“Eh? Motoyasu-kun?”
The carriage rumbled to a halt, and Father climbed down from it.
“It’s been two days. What’s wrong, Motoyasu-kun? Don’t tell me you came to see me off since I’m leaving the country?”
“There are various circumstances at play, indeed. So I’d like you to hear me out for a bit.”
“Eh? Sure…”

Ah, Father—how nostalgic. This was the very first Father from when the loop began, in a sense much like Fleon-chan was to me. I might have already met him while I was in a daze from the shock over Filo-tan, but even so, he was still my Father, I say.
“Father. Up ahead lies a tightly secured checkpoint, and there are those who’ve arranged to kill you the moment you try to leave the country.”
“Eh? Really? Well… given what you and the people of Siltvelt have told me, I figured something like that was possible, but I’d heard things were supposed to go peacefully.”
That would indeed be the case according to the Queen’s instructions. But there were countless people who simply weren’t listening to her.
“So what do we do? Should we take a detour, or sneak out of the country somehow…?”
“No need to worry about that, indeed. I’ve already gone and handled it in a flash.”
That fort was already empty as a husk.
“However, there are various complicated circumstances involved, I say. To tell you the truth, I’ve looped back in time since then.”
“Eh? You looped? What do you mean?”

“It’s a long story, but back then, I was in a situation where the moment any of the Four Cardinal Heroes died, I’d loop right back to right after the summoning. It seems Father must have died somewhere down the line, causing the loop. But this time, I came back to the day before that loop occurred.”
“I see… so there’s a lot of complicated stuff tangled up in this. Then I guess that means you came back through this loop to stop me from being killed.”
“Indeed.”
“In that case… taking into account everything you’ve learned from all these loops, what do you think we should do, Motoyasu-kun?”

Hmm… honestly speaking, the fort was already on the verge of falling, and using the portal, we could reach Siltvelt in an instant. Having reunited with Father meant safety was more or less guaranteed, so there were plenty of options available. Should I just send Father off to Siltvelt as things stood?

Ugh… my memories were a bit hazy on this, but I felt like I should search for a different approach than before. Above all, it might be worth trying out what I’d learned from Father and the others during that previous loop when everyone headed to Faubrey together. Memories of what happened with Ark were also surfacing in my mind. I recalled there being something I mustn’t let Father realize, something I shouldn’t teach him. But there were things I could still discuss with him.
“Father, I know you’re planning to head to Siltvelt, but I’d like you to come with me for now, I say.”
“Sure. If it’s a request from you, Motoyasu-kun, I’m happy to go along with it.”
“Ehh…”
At that, the Siltvelt envoy’s face twisted with visible trouble.
“I apologize for the sudden change of plans, indeed. But if we head straight to Siltvelt as planned, that too would cause problems down the line.”
“What sort of problems, might I ask?”
I explained to the Siltvelt envoy what would happen in the future. Well, as for the matter involving Takt, that I could crush ahead of time.
“It’s an outlandish tale, but I can indeed see it being plausible.”
“If I put my mind to it, I could get us there in an instant, indeed. But could you hold off on heading to Siltvelt for just a little while?”
“An instant… I have heard legends of the Heroes possessing such powers. Understood.”
“Well then, Father, shall we use the portal to rejoin Kuro-chan once more?”
“Sure, got it. Let’s head back for now, then—though it’ll be quite the round trip.”
“Indeed.”

Even as I thought this, I needed to properly sort out what could only be accomplished during this particular loop, right now. I would invite Father to join the party, and bring the Siltvelt envoy along as well.
“Shall we leave the carriage here for the time being?”
“No, I’ll have one of my subordinates deliver it to a nearby town. There’s a chance we might need it again later.”
“Indeed. Well then, let’s be off. Portal Spear!”
Fwoosh! In an instant, we made our round trip back to the castle town of Melromarc.
“Ohh… so this really can get us to Siltvelt in an instant.”
“I wasn’t able to manage that back then, I say.”
Such was the power of information gained through looping.
“It’s like these past two days of travel just vanished in a flash, but… well, I suppose that can’t be helped.”
“What did you do these past two days, Father?”

“After introducing myself to the Siltvelt envoy and their companions, we traveled slowly by carriage. We stopped at an inn along the way, but things got a bit noisy, so we kept moving a few times while staying cautious.”
I see. So a bit of a mix-up had occurred, then.
“Ah, Moto-oh, welcome back!”
Kuro-chan greeted us as we returned to the inn.
“Peep, peep!”
The Filolial-sama chicks greeted us as well. Since we hadn’t leveled up yet, they hadn’t grown at all.
“Oh, it’s Nao. Welcome back!”
“Um…”
Father tilted his head slightly, looking at Kuro-chan. It seemed he couldn’t quite connect Kuro-chan’s angel form with her Filolial form.
“Kuro-chan, why don’t you turn into your Filolial-sama form?”
“Okay!”

With a poof, Kuro-chan transformed into her Filolial form. Her appearance wasn’t all that different from Black Thunder’s. If anything, one might say her eyes gave off a gentler impression than Black Thunder’s.
“Whoa, it really is Kuro-chan!?”
“Yep. Something about the Love Hunter recalling his Destiny, so, nao—he went off chasing his Aegis.”
“Ah… I see. You use some pretty distinctive words, Kuro-chan.”
“Is it cool?”
“Y-yeah, sure. Have you been talking like that for a while now, I wonder…”
Having received words of praise from Father, Kuro-chan smiled happily.
“Filolials really are amazing. You said you were searching for Filo-chan, Motoyasu-kun—how’s that going? Any luck finding her?”
“Of course, I’ve managed to find Filo-tan.”
“That’s good to hear.”
That’s right. Filo-tan was Sakura-chan. And in this loop, Sakura-chan hadn’t hatched yet. Which meant this was a loop where she could still become Filo-tan for me as well.

What fortunate timing, I say. This was the perfect opportunity to try the method Father and the others had taught me during the previous loop—raising Sakura-chan into Filo-tan without hurting Father in the process. To that end, I needed to secure the egg early on. Come to think of it, at this point in time, the egg that would become Filo-tan—Sakura-chan—wasn’t yet at the monster merchant’s shop in Melromarc.
“Now then, time to go retrieve Filo-tan—well, I’d love to say that, but if we simply hatch Filo-tan’s egg as things stand, she won’t become Filo-tan. She’ll become Sakura-chan instead, I say.”
“Is that so?”
“Sakura-chan is a precious Filolial-sama in her own right, as Sakura-chan. But this time, I’d like to try the method for meeting Filo-tan that Father and the others taught me before, indeed.”
